newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-INDIA, TAIWAN CONTINUE TO RETREAT.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-INDIA, TAIWAN CONTINUE TO RETREAT.

text.p: Indian and Taiwanese global depositary receipts continued to retreat on Thursday, following the lead set in home markets where investors pocketed profits after recent advances.
"We've come down following the profit-taking in Bombay but there is no real selling pressure -- it's just market-makers adjusting prices," said one Indian GDR broker.
The HSBC James Capel India GDR index fell 1.03 points, or 1.16 percent, to 88.10, a premium of 21.13 percent to the local market.
Bombay's benchmark 30-share index shed 75.95 to 4,447.06, hit hard by local institutional and speculative selling.
The Taiwanese GDR market also retraced with Taipei, where shares remained hobbled by rising domestic money market rates.
The Capel Taiwan GDR index was off 1.62, or 1.16 percent, at 138.38, a discount of 1.18 percent to Taipei where the weighted index ended off 20.59 at 9,840.88.

The Capel Korea GDR index added 0.37 points, or 0.48 percent, to 77.07, a premium of 46.48 percent to the local market. In Seoul, shares had consolidated with the composite index closing down 0.30 at 745.35.
